description: Provenance manifest for the built-in preset catalog. Each entry pins the template artifact(s) its catalog entry was authored from — the pin is the contract. scripts/preset-drift-check.ts fetches every pinned artifact (hub copies BY COMMIT, never branch head; GGUF copies by repo file, because a re-quantization re-uploads the file and the embedded-template sha is the contract), re-derives the mechanical invariants (docs/design.md, 'Moved from code' — the drift-invariants subsection: the 'Template -> metadata feasibility' table), and diffs them against the catalog entry. sha256 is over the EXACT template text: the hub file bytes, or the GGUF-embedded tokenizer.chat_template string (verified 2026-09 against both the local HF cache and the live resolve endpoint). The tool never writes or suggests preset content: on drift a human re-runs the preset authoring pass (docs/preset-authoring.md) against the new template. Invariants NOT mechanically extractable (spike feasibility table: the level->value cross-vocabulary mapping, the gpt-oss {low,medium,high} vocabulary — prose, not template — and the maxTokens policy) are deliberately NOT asserted here or by the tool.

contracts.note: Hub base repo. Pin == repo head, verified byte-identical 2026-09 (the spike's open question 7: head moved 2026-08-14 but the template stayed identical; re-verified live at drift-check build time).
The sglang deployment repo (server-side copy). Pin == repo head; byte-identical to the base-repo jinja.

What llama-server --jinja serves (GGUF-embedded tokenizer.chat_template, 9993 chars). Diverges from the hub copies by design: 'Unsloth fixes' add a 'high'->'xhigh' alias before the raise-guard (the hub copies RAISE on 'high'). The catalog's effort values (low/medium/xhigh) are valid against both — the drift checker verifies that and reports the divergence as informational, not drift.

The three Qwen 3.6 hub jinjas (27B-FP8, 35B-A3B, 35B-A3B-FP8) were verified byte-identical at authoring (authoring evidence: jj history, v0.2-presets.md §1); both sglang-style (FP8) repos are pinned. Pins == repo heads, verified live 2026-09.
llama-server deployment copy for qwen3.6-27b-mtp. Byte-identical to the 35B-A3B variant below — same template, so one preset, one contract (per-template rule).
The authoring artifact (the only local 3.5 artifact at authoring time). INVERTED enable_thinking polarity vs the hub copy: UNDEFINED enable_thinking = nothink here.

Official hub copy — DIVERGES from the GGUF copy in the UNDEFINED enable_thinking state (hub: undefined -> think; GGUF: undefined -> nothink) and in tool-call argument rendering (|items vs mapping iteration). The catalog's values (explicit boolean, no effort kwarg, no preserve_thinking) are valid against BOTH copies, but the binding must never omit enable_thinking (it does not: no omitWhenOff) — the divergence is contract-relevant in exactly that sense and the checker reports it as informational. Pin == repo head, verified live 2026-09. If a deployment ever serves the hub copy (or a new 3.5 artifact with a different template — docs/preset-authoring.md, 'Known open questions'), re-verify the entry against it.

Standalone jinja (the repo's API metadata embeds NO template — spike). Pin == repo head (2025-08-26), verified live 2026-09. Byte-identical to the GGUF-embedded copy below, so the two pins share one sha.

The deployment artifact (local MXFP4 gguf; KV section sits ~13 MB in, after the vocab arrays). The template does NOT validate reasoning_effort: the {low,medium,high} vocabulary is human-authored from the repo README (prose) — the checker verifies the kwarg name and the 'medium' default, never the vocabulary (spike feasibility table, item 2).
